variants.headline: Looking back: food shortage leaves the colony hungry
variants.sub: People in the colony are hungry because food is insufficient.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: There was not enough food in {colony}, and people were going hungry.

The gazette records insufficient food and hunger as matters of public concern. A shortage and its explanation are distinct subjects, and the public record should not substitute an assumed cause for an established condition. Adequate provision remains the practical measure against which any response ought to be considered.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We support {target} against an automatic adverse judgment. Hunger requires serious attention, but it does not establish every claim about its origin or prove that a particular imagined alternative would meet the need.

variants.headline: Looking back: enough to eat remains the central need
variants.sub: The colony's food supply is insufficient, leaving people hungry.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: People in the colony were hungry because food was insufficient.

The gazette records insufficient food and hunger as matters of public concern. A shortage and its explanation are distinct subjects, and the public record should not substitute an assumed cause for an established condition. Adequate provision remains the practical measure against which any response ought to be considered.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We support {target} against an automatic adverse judgment. Hunger requires serious attention, but it does not establish every claim about its origin or prove that a particular imagined alternative would meet the need.

variants.headline: Looking back: hunger is a fact, not a figure of speech
variants.sub: There is not enough food in {colony}, and people are going hungry.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: The colony's food supply was insufficient, leaving people hungry.

The gazette records insufficient food and hunger as matters of public concern. A shortage and its explanation are distinct subjects, and the public record should not substitute an assumed cause for an established condition. Adequate provision remains the practical measure against which any response ought to be considered.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We support {target} against an automatic adverse judgment. Hunger requires serious attention, but it does not establish every claim about its origin or prove that a particular imagined alternative would meet the need.
